lines: A module is delivered more than once inside a single page:
libresign-init: 12,022 B beyond the first copy, @nextcloud/files 11,057 B, @nextcloud/paths 681 B, @nextcloud/sharing 284 B.
All 6 pages load the same 1 file: 198,563 B raw, 73,954 B gzip, 54.9 % of the smallest page (libresign-tab, 361,740 B).
Inside: @vue/runtime-core 62,637 B, vite-plugin-node-polyfills 29,432 B, dompurify 24,421 B, @vue/runtime-dom 23,515 B, @vue/reactivity 17,736 B.
moment, 292,378 B on the libresign-main page: carries its locale data; luxon and date-fns are a fraction of it.
vite-plugin-node-polyfills, 57,468 B on the libresign-main page: Node APIs polyfilled into a browser bundle.
No package is imported as a whole: every package contributes only the modules that are used (202 packages, 904 modules).
On this measure the form of importing is exhausted. A root import whose barrel the bundler removes completely leaves no trace, so this is evidence, not proof.
No bundler chunk in js and css is left without something that loads it.
